title: JAPAN'S GREATEST SORCERER WAS HALF FOX
subtitle: Kuzunoha, the fox mother
source: Kuzunoha legend (Shinoda Forest, Izumi; the 1734 puppet play Ashiya Doman Ouchi Kagami and earlier tales); Abe no Seimei (921-1005), onmyoji of the Heian court; Kuzunoha Inari Shrine, Izumi, Osaka; Seimei Shrine, Kyoto.

lines.say: [storytelling, low] The most powerful sorcerer in Japanese history... was half fox.
A thousand years ago, a young man named Yasuna was walking through Shinoda Forest, when hunters chased a white fox right into his arms.
He hid it. The hunters beat him for it. And the fox got away.
[gentle] That night, a beautiful woman found him hurt by the road. Her name was Kuzunoha.
cap: found him hurt by the road.

lines.say: She nursed him back to health. They fell in love. They married. They had a son.
cap: She nursed him back to health.

lines.say: [warm] For six years, they were the happiest family in Izumi.
[beat] But here's the thing. Foxes can't hide forever.
[quiet] One morning, their little boy looked at his mother... and saw a tail.
[sad] She couldn't stay. A fox who has been seen must go home. Before she left, she wrote a poem on the paper door.
cap: A fox who has been seen

lines.say: [softly] If you miss me, come find me, in the forest of Shinoda.
[sniffling] Did they ever see her again?
[gentle] They searched the forest. She came out one last time, as a white fox, and gave her son a crystal orb.
cap: and gave her son a {o:crystal orb}.

lines.say: With it, he could hear the voices of animals, and see spirits no one else could.
[proud] That boy grew up to be Abe no Seimei. The greatest onmyoji who ever lived.
cap: That boy grew up to be

lines.say: [smug] Every fox in Japan says yes.
